findings.body: The FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle has no observable effect: both branches of the conditional return false, so SQL Expressions can never be re-enabled through the toggle even though the toggle is retained in the codebase for that purpose, and the dead branch misleads future maintainers into thinking flag state is evaluated.
findings.failure_mode: Dead/unreachable conditional branch silently defeats the purpose of the feature-flag check, misleading reviewers and future maintainers about the toggle's effect.
findings.impact: The FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle has no observable effect: both branches of the conditional return false, so SQL Expressions can never be re-enabled through the toggle even though the toggle is retained in the codebase for that purpose, and the dead branch misleads future maintainers into thinking flag state is evaluated.
findings.root_cause: The negated flag value is computed and branched on, but both branches unconditionally return false, leaving no code path where the flag state actually changes the outcome.
findings.suggested_fix: Simplify the function to `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` if the flag is meant to eventually re-enable the feature, or replace it with a hardcoded `return false` and a comment explaining the permanent disablement, removing the dead branch.
findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the FlagSqlExpressions toggle a dead check
findings.trigger: Any invocation of enableSqlExpressions(h), regardless of whether FlagSqlExpressions is enabled or disabled via feature toggle configuration.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch adds enableSqlExpressions at lines 194-200 with both branches returning false regardless of the flag value. The code `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions); if enabled { return false } return false` makes the feature toggle completely ineffective - the function always returns false. This is a real bug where the conditional is dead code.

pr.body:
<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

Remove reference to DuckDB

**Why do we need this feature?**

See the blog post describing the vulnerability, for which a fix was rolled out to all Grafana versions earlier today:
https://grafana.com/blog/2024/10/17/grafana-security-release-critical-severity-fix-for-cve-2024-9264/

The full extent of our documentation around this feature seems to be here:
https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/81666/files#diff-16fb71b28e5b6197615abba8a07bc73d9bf75ebc60311663e1c29976de5cc9a6

All we've documented is that the feature-flag exists. That flag still exists in the codebase, so I'm tempted not to touch that documentation for now. We can always follow up with more improvements after this PR.

**Who is this feature for?**

Everyone

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

This moves the security fix into Grafana repo itself, now that it has been publicly announced. We need this here so we can clean up and simplify our Security-releases pipeline once again.

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
   Behaviour of this patch was already verified manually by @toddtreece. See his confirmation of this on our private slack, [here](https://raintank-corp.slack.com/archives/C07P60RBAUD/p1727902629844259?thread_ts=1727901896.911799&cid=C07P60RBAUD)
   Tested again on the Ephemeral instance here: https://ephemeral1511182194942samjewe.grafana-dev.net/d/be18gem24w2dcf/test-sql-expressions-bugfix?from=now-1h&to=now&timezone=browser
- [ ] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc.
pr.title: ServerSideExpressions: Disable SQL Expressions to prevent RCE and LFI vulnerability

raw_findings.body: The FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle has no observable effect: both branches of the conditional return false, so SQL Expressions can never be re-enabled through the toggle even though the toggle is retained in the codebase for that purpose, and the dead branch misleads future maintainers into thinking flag state is evaluated.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Dead/unreachable conditional branch silently defeats the purpose of the feature-flag check, misleading reviewers and future maintainers about the toggle's effect.
raw_findings.impact: The FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle has no observable effect: both branches of the conditional return false, so SQL Expressions can never be re-enabled through the toggle even though the toggle is retained in the codebase for that purpose, and the dead branch misleads future maintainers into thinking flag state is evaluated.
raw_findings.root_cause: The negated flag value is computed and branched on, but both branches unconditionally return false, leaving no code path where the flag state actually changes the outcome.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Simplify the function to `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` if the flag is meant to eventually re-enable the feature, or replace it with a hardcoded `return false` and a comment explaining the permanent disablement, removing the dead branch.
raw_findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the FlagSqlExpressions toggle a dead check
raw_findings.trigger: Any invocation of enableSqlExpressions(h), regardless of whether FlagSqlExpressions is enabled or disabled via feature toggle configuration.

raw_findings.body: Regressions in the SQL-expression disablement logic (the core security fix of this PR) would not be caught by the existing test suite in pkg/expr/reader_test.go.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent regression of the security-critical disablement path due to lack of automated test verification.
raw_findings.impact: Regressions in the SQL-expression disablement logic (the core security fix of this PR) would not be caught by the existing test suite in pkg/expr/reader_test.go.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces new branching logic for QueryTypeSQL without adding corresponding unit test coverage in the existing reader_test.go table-driven tests.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a test case to pkg/expr/reader_test.go that constructs a QueryTypeSQL query and asserts ReadQuery returns the 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error for both feature-flag-enabled and feature-flag-disabled ExpressionQueryReader instances.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage added for new QueryTypeSQL disablement branch in ReadQuery
raw_findings.trigger: A future refactor of enableSqlExpressions or the QueryTypeSQL branch that regresses the intended 'always disabled' behavior would go undetected because reader_test.go has no test case exercising QueryTypeSQL.

finding.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage observation, not a defect in the patch itself. The candidate claims missing test coverage is a bug, but absence of tests is a quality/process concern, not a functional defect introduced by the patch. The patch's behavior (always disabling SQL expressions) is intentional per the PR context, and lack of test coverage doesn't constitute a bug in the changed code.
